text:
Sampled softmax is a plausible replacement for sampled BCE while retaining masked-target BERT4Rec. The 2024 [gSASRec study](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) links sampled BCE to overconfidence and training instability; this supports investigating the objective without changing backbone. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) directly addresses in-batch sampling bias: frequent items appear disproportionately as negatives. Standard logQ adjusts logits by sampling probability, but mishandles the deterministically included positive. The refined derivation treats positive and negative contributions separately and introduces an uncertainty-dependent weight. Its evidence concerns retrieval and other sequential architectures, so transfer to masked BERT4Rec remains a hypothesis.

Sampling correction and false-negative handling solve different problems. [Prakash et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) find dataset-dependent accuracy/popularity trade-offs across uniform, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling. [SID4SRec (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950705126010221) reports benefits from filtering semantically overlapping contrastive negatives, but does not establish the same benefit for masked-item softmax. A conservative experiment would remove target collisions and known training-positive negatives, derive probabilities for the actual filtered sampler, and avoid treating merely high-scoring items as confirmed positives.

Computationally, [Batch Size or Negatives? (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11061) describes reducing output-logit memory from O(BV) to O(BK) with K sampled candidates. Proposed experiment: one BERT4Rec per category, corrected mixed uniform/in-batch sampled softmax at masked positions, appended-mask inference using raw model scores. Preserve the evaluator; select negative count and sampling mix using macro validation HR@10 and measured GPU cost.
